## 1. First-conjugation imperfect

Rule: For regular first-conjugation verbs, form the imperfect active indicative from the present stem, the imperfect marker and the active personal ending.
Applicability: Regular first-conjugation verbs, imperfect indicative active.
Caveat: Check first-person singular ending adjustments separately; this is not a rule for every Latin verb.
Example: amābam — first-person singular imperfect active indicative.
Course memory aid (German): Mit ba war es damals da.

## 2. Rule without a memory aid

Rule: In a regular first-declension noun, the genitive plural ends in -ārum.
Applicability: Regular first-declension genitive plural.
Caveat: Do not infer a noun's declension from this ending rule alone.
No course memory aid is supplied. Do not fabricate one.
